messages:
sam: Quick design review — I mocked a compact CIDR suggestion inside the Connect step. Screenshot + frames in Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE. TL;DR: show a small, non-obtrusive suggestion when someone types a single IPv4 address (suggest /24). Keep it keyboard-first and a11y-friendly.

eva: Nice idea. My main worry is layout shift on small screens — if the suggestion appears below the input it can push the confirm button offscreen. Can we make it overlay or reserve space?

mike: Agree with eva. Also keyboard behaviour: suggestion must not steal focus. Pressing Tab should move to the next form control, and arrow keys should let you pick the suggested CIDR if the user toggles it.

ashley: Copy suggestion: instead of the very terse 'Suggested CIDR', how about 'Recommended subnet (editable)'? Slightly clearer for folks who aren’t infra-native. For very small viewports we can abbreviate to 'Subnet (rec)'.

sam: Good calls. Accessibility note: the suggestion chip should be reachable via keyboard and announced when it appears. Use aria-live='polite' so screen readers hear it but aren’t interrupted.

aria-bot: a11y quick checklist: 1) helper region with aria-live='polite' + role='status' for short announcements; 2) suggestion must have focusable attribute (tabindex=0) and visible focus ring; 3) tooltip / 'Why this?' must be reachable by keyboard and have aria-describedby linking to the explanation.

mike: Implementation snippet (CSS reference):
```
.suggestion-chip{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;padding:4px 8px;border-radius:999px;background:#f3f4f6;border:1px solid #e5e7eb;font-size:14px;}
@media(max-width:480px){.suggestion-chip{font-size:12px;padding:3px 6px;}}
```
Keep it visually light so it’s not mistaken for an error.

eva: UX nit — add a tiny 'Why this?' affordance (question icon) that opens a short popover explaining: 'Defaulting to /24 keeps most customer networks reachable while avoiding huge CIDR ranges that cause routing problems.' Popover must be dismissible with Esc.

ashley: Error-state copy suggestion: when user picks a range that overlaps our reserved nets show: 'We can’t accept 10.0.0.0/8 — this range is reserved. Try 10.0.1.0/24 or choose a different subnet.' Keep the language actionable (exact example + next step).

sam: Telemetry question — can we add a single opt-in flag to event when users accept the suggestion (no IPs in logs, just boolean accepted_suggestion=true) so Product can validate usefulness? Should be off by default in private deployments unless customer opts in.

mike: Sounds good. Also drop shadow on the suggestion chip is probably overkill; prefer a 1px border and subtle background. If we add an icon, make it decorative with aria-hidden='true'.

eva: OK I’ll update the Figma frames: overlay vs inline variants, and a keyboard-flow prototype. Planning an a11y lab tomorrow at 11am PT — @ashley can you bring the tooltip copy?

ashley: On it — drafting two lengths: 80-char short (for tooltip) and 220-char full explanation for docs. Will drop both here by EOD :memo:.

deploy-bot: Screenshot uploaded to Figma and link posted in the pinned messages channel. Quick reminder: label any changes that affect tab order as 'a11y-impact' in the PR.

sam: Awesome — thanks everyone. Once eva posts the updated frames I’ll file a small UX ticket with acceptance criteria (keyboard nav, aria-live, telemetry flag).
